title: Mahsa Amini Protests
description: Nationwide uprising following the death of Mahsa Amini in morality police custody. Largest protest wave since 1979 revolution, spanning 160+ cities. Security forces killed over 500 protesters.

title: Green Movement Uprising
description: Mass protests erupted after disputed 2009 presidential election. Millions marched in Tehran and other cities demanding annulment of results. Regime crackdown killed dozens and imprisoned hundreds.

title: November 2019 Fuel Price Protests
description: Protests erupted across Iran after government announced sudden 50-300% fuel price hike. Spread to 100+ cities within 48 hours. Internet was shut down nationally for 6 days.

title: December 2017 Economic Protests
description: Spontaneous protests erupted across 80+ Iranian cities over economic hardship, unemployment, and corruption. Chants included 'Death to the dictator' targeting Khamenei directly for the first time. IRGC deployed to suppress protests.

title: 2021 Khuzestan Water Crisis Protests
description: Residents of Khuzestan province took to streets over severe water shortages and mismanagement. At least 8 people killed by security forces. Protests spread to other cities in solidarity with Arab-Iranian minority.

title: Teachers and Workers General Strikes 2018-2019
description: Teachers, truck drivers, sugarcane workers and bazaar merchants staged coordinated nationwide strikes demanding higher wages. Over 1,000 arrested. Strikes marked emergence of organized labor resistance against the regime.

title: 2024 Post-Election Protest Wave
description: Despite nominal election of reformist Pezeshkian, activists documented ongoing street protests over economic conditions and political repression. Civil society groups called for boycotts with lowest-ever turnout in several cities.

title: Mahsa Amini Protest Crackdown - 500+ Killed
description: IRGC and Basij systematically shot protesters across 160+ cities. Amnesty International documented over 500 killed. Thousands imprisoned. Executions of protest-linked detainees followed in 2023.

title: Record 853 Executions in 2023
description: Iran executed at least 853 people in 2023, the highest number in 15 years and one of the highest globally. Many were related to protest convictions under vague national security charges.

title: Bloody November 2019 - Approximately 1500 Killed
description: Security forces killed an estimated 1,500 protesters in six days during the November 2019 uprising according to Reuters citing official sources. The true toll remains unknown due to information blackout.

title: First Executions of Mahsa Amini Protesters
description: Iran executed Mohsen Shekari and Mohammad Mehdi Karami in December 2022 for their role in the protests, the first protest-related executions. International condemnation intensified. Iran pressed ahead with further executions of protesters in 2023.

title: Iran Executions Exceed 700 in 2024
description: Iran surpassed 700 executions by mid-2024, on track for a record year. Death sentences issued under 'Spreading Corruption on Earth' charges against protesters, journalists, and dissidents. UN experts condemned escalation as judicial terror.

title: 2009 Post-Election Torture and Executions
description: Following Green Movement suppression, detainees at Kahrizak detention center were tortured and raped. At least 3 died under torture. Show trials of reformists televised. Dozens executed under national security charges over following years.

title: US Withdrawal from JCPOA Nuclear Deal
description: President Trump announced withdrawal from the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action and reimposed sweeping sanctions. Iran called it a violation of international law. Nuclear deal effectively collapsed.

title: Iran Enriches Uranium to 60% Purity
description: Iran announced it had enriched uranium to 60% purity, a significant step toward weapons-grade 90%. Declared in response to sabotage at Natanz facility. IAEA confirmed the enrichment.

title: Iran Reaches 84% Uranium Enrichment
description: IAEA inspectors detected uranium particles enriched to 84% at Fordow. Iran denied intentional breach, attributing it to technical fluctuations. 84% is near weapons-grade threshold of 90%.

title: Iran Begins Industrial-Scale Uranium Enrichment at Natanz
description: President Ahmadinejad announced Iran had successfully enriched uranium using 164 centrifuges. Defied UN Security Council demands to halt enrichment. Crossed threshold from research to industrial-scale program. International sanctions escalation began.

title: Natanz Advanced Centrifuge Hall Destroyed by Sabotage
description: A major explosion destroyed the advanced centrifuge assembly hall at Natanz facility, widely attributed to Israeli intelligence. Iran accelerated enrichment in response, announcing installation of IR-6 advanced centrifuges 10x faster than IR-1. Triggered direct escalation cycle.

title: Iran Accumulates 128kg of 60% Enriched Uranium
description: IAEA reported Iran had accumulated 128.3 kg of uranium enriched to 60% purity by late 2023, enough for two nuclear weapons if further enriched. With 84% particle detection and monitoring gaps, experts calculated Iran's breakout timeline at under 2 weeks.

title: Iran Installs Advanced IR-6 Centrifuges at Fordow
description: Iran notified IAEA it was installing advanced IR-6 centrifuges at the deeply buried Fordow facility, which is immune to conventional bunker-buster strikes. The move dramatically increased enrichment capacity and signaled Iran was hardening its nuclear sites against military attack.

title: Iran Seizes British Tanker Stena Impero in Strait of Hormuz
description: IRGC Navy commandos fast-roped onto the UK-flagged Stena Impero and seized it in the Strait of Hormuz. UK scrambled warships. Tanker held for 65 days as leverage in diplomatic dispute.

title: Limpet Mine Attacks on Oil Tankers Near Fujairah
description: Multiple oil tankers attacked using limpet mines near the UAE port of Fujairah. US and Saudi Arabia attributed attacks to Iran. Two tankers severely damaged. Created global maritime insurance crisis.

title: Iranian-Backed Houthi Attacks on Red Sea Shipping
description: Yemen-based Houthis, armed and directed by Iran, launched sustained drone and missile attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea. Forced major shipping rerouting around Cape of Good Hope. Significant global supply chain disruption.

title: Iran Drone Attack Kills Security Guard on MV Mercer Street
description: A one-way attack drone struck the Israeli-managed tanker MV Mercer Street in the Gulf of Oman, killing a British and Romanian crew member. US, UK, and Israel attributed the attack to Iran. First Iran drone attack to kill Western nationals on a commercial vessel.

title: IRGC Seizes MSC Aries Container Ship in Strait of Hormuz
description: IRGC commandos rappelled from a helicopter to seize the MSC Aries, a Portugal-flagged container ship with 25 crew, in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran held the vessel for months. Marked the largest commercial vessel seizure by Iran and directly threatened global container shipping.

title: IRGC Boats Attempt to Board HMS Montrose
description: IRGC patrol boats attempted to intercept and board the British-flagged Heritage oil tanker but were warned off by HMS Montrose. Iran denied the incident. Occurred during peak Hormuz tensions. Escalated naval confrontation in the world's most critical oil chokepoint.

title: Iran Mines Gulf Waters, Disrupts Global Oil Flows
description: Iran deployed naval mines in the Persian Gulf region as part of a gray-zone pressure campaign. CENTCOM tracked increased IRGC mine-laying activities near international shipping lanes. Disrupted 20% of world oil transit through Hormuz.

title: Stuxnet Worm Destroys Natanz Centrifuges
description: The Stuxnet cyberweapon, widely attributed to US-Israeli intelligence, physically destroyed approximately 1,000 Iranian uranium enrichment centrifuges at Natanz. First known cyberweapon to cause physical destruction.

title: Cyberattack Paralyzes Iranian Fuel Distribution Network
description: A major cyberattack, attributed to Israel-linked group Predatory Sparrow, took down Iran's national fuel distribution network. Over 4,300 petrol stations went offline. Regime accused of cover-up.

title: Shamoon Malware Destroys 30,000 Saudi Aramco Workstations
description: Iran-linked hackers deployed the Shamoon malware against Saudi Aramco, destroying 30,000 computer workstations in hours. Most destructive cyberattack on a private company in history at the time. Demonstrated Iran's willingness to conduct destructive cyber operations against critical infrastructure.

title: US DOJ Indicts Iranian Hackers for Power Grid and Dam Attacks
description: US Justice Department indicted Iranian hackers for targeting US power grids, water systems, and a New York dam control system. Iranian APT groups also breached networks of US financial institutions. First indictment explicitly naming IRGC-linked hackers for attacks on critical infrastructure.

title: Iran APT MuddyWater Compromises US Federal Networks
description: CISA and FBI issued joint alert that Iranian state-sponsored MuddyWater group actively targeted US, UK, and European government networks. Campaigns focused on espionage and pre-positioning for destructive attacks. Over 50 US government agencies affected.

title: Iran Escalates Cyber Operations Against US and Israel in 2024
description: CISA and NSA documented a surge in Iranian cyber operations targeting US defense contractors, Israeli water infrastructure, and Albanian government systems. IRGC Cyber Command expanded its offensive toolkit with custom wiper malware. Election interference operations also documented.

title: Gonjeshke Darande Attacks Iran Steel Plants and Rail Network
description: Hacktivist group Gonjeshke Darande, linked to Israeli intelligence, disrupted operations at three Iranian steel plants and Iran's national rail system. Steel plant attacks caused fires visible on satellite imagery. First known destructive attack on Iranian heavy industry.

title: US Drone Strike Assassinates IRGC General Qasem Soleimani
description: US airstrike at Baghdad airport killed IRGC Quds Force commander Qasem Soleimani and Iraqi PMF commander Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. Most significant direct US-Iran military action in decades. Iran vowed revenge.

title: Iran Fires 16 Ballistic Missiles at US Bases in Iraq
description: Iran launched 16 ballistic missiles at Al-Assad and Erbil air bases in Iraq hosting US forces. First direct Iranian state-on-state ballistic missile attack on US military. Over 100 US personnel suffered traumatic brain injuries.

title: Iran Launches Operation True Promise I - 300 Drones and Missiles at Israel
description: Iran launched over 300 drones and missiles directly at Israel from Iranian soil, the first direct state-on-state attack between Iran and Israel. Over 99% intercepted by US, UK, French, Jordanian, and Israeli forces. Marked historic escalation.

title: Hezbollah-Israel War 2006 - Iran Proves Proxy Deterrence
description: Hezbollah, armed and funded by Iran's IRGC, fought Israel to a military stalemate in 34 days. Hezbollah fired over 4,000 rockets into Israel, including precision-guided missiles supplied by Iran. Demonstrated Iran's ability to project military deterrence through proxies without direct exposure.

title: Iran Shoots Down US RQ-4A Global Hawk Surveillance Drone
description: Iran's IRGC shot down a US Navy RQ-4A Global Hawk drone worth $220 million over the Strait of Hormuz using a surface-to-air missile. US disputed Iran's claim it was in Iranian airspace. President Trump initially authorized retaliatory strikes before canceling minutes before launch.

title: Iran Launches Operation True Promise II - 200 Ballistic Missiles at Israel
description: Iran fired approximately 200 ballistic missiles at Israel in retaliation for Israeli strikes on Iranian territory. Several missiles impacted Israeli military bases including Nevatim Air Base. Israel vowed direct retaliation. Represented the most significant conventional ballistic missile barrage in modern warfare history.

title: Hardliner Ebrahim Raisi Wins Presidential Election
description: Ebrahim Raisi, linked to the 1988 mass executions of political prisoners, won Iran's presidential election after reformist candidates were disqualified. Lowest voter turnout in Islamic Republic history. Marked consolidation of hardliner control.

title: IAEA Board Censures Iran, Cuts Monitoring Access
description: IAEA Board of Governors voted to censure Iran for lack of cooperation. Iran responded by disconnecting 27 IAEA monitoring cameras, creating a massive intelligence blind spot on nuclear activities.

title: Ahmadinejad Elected, Declares Nuclear Defiance
description: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad won Iran's presidency on platform of anti-Western defiance. Declared Iran would never abandon its nuclear program regardless of UN pressure. Ended diplomatic opening of Khatami era. Set Iran on confrontational path that led to maximum sanctions regime.

title: JCPOA Revival Talks Collapse Under Raisi Government
description: Negotiations to revive the 2015 nuclear deal broke down after Iran demanded removal of IRGC from US terror list and guarantees no future president could leave. US walked away from near-final deal in August 2022. Diplomatic path to resolving nuclear crisis closed.

title: President Raisi Killed in Helicopter Crash, Hardliner Succession Secured
description: President Raisi and Foreign Minister Amir-Abdollahian died in helicopter crash in fog-shrouded mountains. Khamenei declared 5 days of mourning. Despite nominal election of reformist Pezeshkian, hardliners retained full control of IRGC, judiciary, and parliament. Khamenei's succession dynamics accelerated.

title: Iran-Russia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
description: Iran and Russia signed a 20-year Comprehensive Strategic Partnership covering defense, energy, trade, and technology. Iran supplied Russia with Shahed drones and ballistic missiles for use in Ukraine. Russia provided advanced air defense systems and Su-35 jets to Iran. New axis fundamentally altered regional power balance.

title: Khamenei Signals Nuclear Doctrine Shift, Fatwa Under Review
description: Senior IRGC commanders and regime ideologists publicly floated reversing Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons. State media carried analyses arguing weapons capability was now religiously permissible given existential threats. Intelligence assessments indicated Iran was within weeks of weapons-grade material.

title: Iranian Rial Collapses 80% Under Sanctions
description: The Iranian rial lost approximately 80% of its value as US and EU sanctions tightened. Oil exports halved. Imports of medicine and basic goods severely disrupted. Middle class wealth effectively destroyed.

title: Iran Annual Inflation Exceeds 40% Under Maximum Pressure
description: Following US maximum pressure campaign sanctions, Iran's annual inflation rate exceeded 40% with food inflation reaching 60%+. Unemployment and poverty rates surged. IMF cited as among world's worst economic contractions.

title: Iranian Rial Hits Historic Low, 600,000 per USD
description: The Iranian rial reached a new historic low of approximately 600,000 rials per US dollar in 2023, compared to 32,000 per dollar in 2011. Purchasing power of ordinary Iranians collapsed. Black market premiums widespread.

title: Iran Oil Exports Collapse to Near Zero Under Maximum Pressure
description: US maximum pressure sanctions reduced Iran's oil exports from 2.5 million barrels/day to under 300,000 bpd by mid-2019. Lost approximately $200 billion in oil revenues over four years. Budget deficit forced withdrawal from sovereign wealth funds and social program cuts.

title: 60% of Iranians Living Below Poverty Line by 2023
description: Iranian parliamentary research center reported 60% of Iranians living below the absolute poverty line by 2023, up from 25% in 2010. Youth unemployment above 25%. Brain drain accelerated with 150,000+ skilled professionals emigrating annually. UN identified structural collapse in social safety net.

title: Iran 2022 Budget Deficit Crisis and Currency Collapse
description: Iran's 2022 budget was based on oil price assumptions 60% above actual export revenues, creating structural deficit. Government resorted to printing money, accelerating inflation to 52%. Foreign exchange reserves fell to levels insufficient to cover 3 months of imports.
